column1: # Turkish stress exceptions — word<TAB>1-based stressed syllable (default is final).
# Mined from kaikki.org Turkish (Wiktionary, CC-BY-SA): entries whose stress-marked IPA puts primary
# stress on a NON-final syllable, orthographic-syllable-count-gated (2,103 words). Replaces an earlier
# seeded list (244 entries; 167/171 position agreement on the overlap). CC-BY-SA-derived; referee-circularity
# caveat: the tr referee (wikipron) shares Wiktionary parentage.
# ⚠ REFRESHED (#1569) against the kaikki dump of 2026-10-14. A Wiktionary page lists every reading of a spelling,
# so a possessive's page also carries the PREDICATIVE (adım 'my name' / 'it is my name') and a verbal noun's the
# NEGATIVE IMPERATIVE (okuma 'reading' / 'don't read'). The original mine kept the non-final variant; 505 rows where
# a possessive, case or verbal-noun sense exists now hold the page's FIRST-listed reading, the commoner one in
# running text, and 10 rows matching no kaikki variant take kaikki's. Kept: 33 rows whose pages disagree on the
# first reading (akım, arama, koyun), 122 genuine variants with no inflectional explanation (artık, ama, acilen),
# and trabzon (a place name: Sezer stress, as roma/goma below). Generated by a probe, not typed.
# ── Adjudicated additions (in-repo human-authored facts; not from any single upstream) ──
# Emphatic-reduplication intensives are initial-stressed (Göksel & Kerslake, Turkish: A
# Comprehensive Grammar §4.3.2); 2-syllable place names are initial-stressed (Sezer stress);
# avrupa/iyice are documented lexical exceptions. Entries the kaikki mine lacked but whose
# ── FINAL-stress rows: words the pre-accenting -mA / -sA / -(y)lA rule mis-stresses (#1523) ──
# turkish.ts anchors those three suffixes only at the word END, so a plain noun that merely ends in
# -mA/-sA/-lA took the rule (elma → *ˈelma*, masa → *mˈasa*). Measured against kaikki.org Turkish
# (Wiktionary, CC-BY-SA; the same source as the rows above) over its 9,819 unambiguous stress-marked
# words: the three arms cost 205 words and earned 5 (pırasa, fransa, fanila, haliyle, haşema). But kaikki
# is a DICTIONARY, and the arms earn their keep on running text it does not cover — the conditional
# (olsa), the instrumental (nedeniyle), negation (olmadan) — so the arms stay and the 205 words are listed.
# Each row is a word kaikki marks with exactly one FINAL stress that the rule moves; a word kaikki gives two
# readings (gelme: verbal noun against negative imperative) is left to the rule. The value is the final
# syllable, the default the rule overrode. Generated by a probe over the kaikki dump, not typed.
# #1551: the pre-accent rule was narrowed to the suffixes its sources list (see turkish.ts). These rows are every
# unambiguous kaikki word the NARROWED rule still mis-stresses, plus ten (pırasa, fransa, katır …) the old rule had
# read right only by misfiring: roots that merely end in the letters of a suffix (kültür, nadir, çadır, takdir) and
# place names (Altınyayla). Each value is the word's single kaikki stress (kaikki.org Turkish, Wiktionary, CC-BY-SA;
# dump of 2026-10-14), generated by a probe over that dump, not typed. The five negative participles kaikki lists
# as lexicalised adjectives (istenmeyen, giyilmemiş …) are left to the rule, which follows the sources' verbal
# #1551: two PLACE NAMES the old rule stressed right only by misfiring on -mA. Turkish place names take Sezer stress
# (Sezer 1981; summarised in en.wikipedia "Turkish phonology"): never the final syllable, so a two-syllable name
# stresses its first. Neither is in kaikki.
# #1551: UNSOURCED, KEPT AS THEY WERE. Four frequent FLEURS words (fazla ×92, ise ×34, mesela ×12, kimse ×8) the old
# rule pre-stressed and the narrowed one would make final. No source marks their stress either way: kaikki has no
# entry, en.wiktionary gives /fɑzɫɑ/ and /me.se.laː/ with no stress mark, tr.wiktionary none, and `kimse` has only
# an audio file. Moving ~150 tokens of common words on no evidence is the wrong default, so the old reading is
# preserved here, explicitly as unsourced. Replace any row with a sourced value when one is found.
# ⚠ 2026-10-15: CLASS RULES FOUND, NOT WORD ATTESTATIONS. Halit Dursunoğlu, "Türkiye Türkçesinde Vurgu", pp. 270–273
# (https://dergipark.org.tr/tr/download/article-file/31986), states three tendencies, not word entries:
#   §A.6.3 the conditional -se, from "ise", is pre-stressing: gelecékse, yazársa;
#   §B.3   "zarfların çoğunda" (in most adverbs) the stress is on the first syllable: yárın, sónra, yíne, şímdi;
#   §B.4   "bağlaçlarda çoğunlukla" (in conjunctions, mostly) on the first: çünkü, yáhut, yálnız.
# fazla 1 (adverb), ise 1 (conjunction; i- + the pre-stressing -se) and kimse 1 (kim + -se) AGREE with them.
# mesela 2 does NOT: as an adverb, §B.3 would put it on syllable 1. It is left at 2, because a "most adverbs"
# tendency does not settle one Arabic loan; it needs a word-level source (a stress-marking dictionary, or audio).
